name: Famine
value: Famine risk in 13 Sudan areas; none confirmed
summary: FAO and WFP flag famine risk in 13 Sudan areas on 27 Nov; no area newly classified as Famine (IPC Phase 5)
state: The FAO–WFP Hunger Hotspots report of 27 Nov warns of a risk of famine in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January 2027 under a worst-case scenario, notes two South Darfur displacement camps with acute malnutrition above famine thresholds, and flags famine risk in four South Sudan counties (allAfrica). It lists Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, parts of Nigeria and Yemen as highest concern. No area was newly classified as Famine as of 27 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Famine risk is concentrated in conflict zones where aid access is blocked. Rising hunger tends to drive further displacement and disease outbreaks, and increases pressure on humanitarian appeals and neighbouring countries.
rubric_hit: Watch: risk of famine alerts — FAO–WFP flag famine risk in 13 Sudan areas (27 Nov); no new IPC Phase 5 classification

why: Famine is the most extreme humanitarian failure, almost always man-made by conflict.
drivers: War, sieges, aid access, harvest failure, funding cuts.
